records.reference_transcript: Habari team, this is Grace Wanjiru, the CHV from Rongai. I want to report on today's family planning outreach at Kampi ya Moto dispensary. We started at nine in the morning with a short talk on the different methods, then the nurse, Sister Mary Chebet, gave services. In total, forty-two women came, and most of them were young mothers. Six women were referred to Rongai Health Centre for implants because we ran out of stock. One mama asked to be called for follow-up, her number is 0711 000 482. I will send the register tomorrow. Thank you.

records.reference_transcript: Hi team, Beatrice Atieno here, reporting from the Tumaini women's group meeting in Mogotio. Today was our monthly table banking day. Twenty-five members attended out of thirty. Together they saved eighteen thousand shillings, and we gave out four small loans to members who are starting businesses, mostly selling vegetables and second-hand clothes. The treasurer, Mama Lucy Kiprop, recorded everything in the book. Our next meeting is on the fifteenth. If you need the records, Lucy's number is 0745 000 638.

records.reference_transcript: Morning everyone, this is Janet Mwangi. Yesterday we went to Sarambei Primary School for the menstrual hygiene session with the girls in class six to eight. Sixty girls attended. We talked about periods, how to use and dispose of pads safely, and why they should not miss school. At the end, every girl received a pack of reusable sanitary pads. The head teacher, Mrs. Esther Koech, has asked us to come back and also talk to the mothers. Her phone number is 0790 000 274 if someone wants to follow up.

records.reference_transcript: Hello team, it's Mercy Wambui. I want to share about the community dialogue on gender-based violence we held this afternoon at the chief's camp in Solai. Thirty-five women attended, plus a few village elders. The police gender desk officer, Corporal Ann Mutua, explained how to report cases and where survivors can get help. Some women shared their stories, it was very emotional. Three women asked for private follow-up, and we connected them with the counsellor. For anything about this session, you can call me on 0701 000 593.

I will upload the full report later.

records.reference_transcript: Hello team, this is Caroline Nyambura reporting from Kampi ya Moto. Today we held the kitchen garden training for women farmers. Eighteen women attended. The agriculture officer, Mr. Peter Langat, showed them how to make a sack garden and how to make compost from kitchen waste. Each woman received seedlings of sukuma wiki and spinach to plant at home. Next month we will visit their homes to see how the gardens are doing. If you want to join the follow-up visits, call me on 0712 000 765.
